name: Health Assist
description: Simple App Store screenshots: one app screen and four feature text panels.

elements.name: body
elements.content: The app reads Apple Health on your iPhone and sends the readings to a webhook in your Home Assistant. There is no account and no service in the middle.

elements.name: footer
elements.content: HEALTH ASSIST · APPLE HEALTH → HOME ASSISTANT

elements.name: body
elements.content: Health Assist does not relay data through a cloud. The phone has to be able to open the webhook URL itself: the same Wi-Fi, a VPN such as Tailscale, or a remote address such as Nabu Casa. If the phone cannot reach that address, the sync fails.

elements.name: footer
elements.content: HEALTH ASSIST · APPLE HEALTH → HOME ASSISTANT

elements.name: body
elements.content: Steps, sleep, heart rate, weight and other readings become Home Assistant sensors. The first sync sends all available history; later syncs send new data. Sensors have stable IDs and units, and history is added to long-term statistics.

elements.name: footer
elements.content: HEALTH ASSIST · APPLE HEALTH → HOME ASSISTANT

elements.name: body
elements.content: The app and the integration are free and MIT licensed. There is no account, no analytics, no paid tier and no in-app purchase. If you want to support it, Sponsor My Work is optional and unlocks nothing.
